- [LLEX.11.2.4] **A float literal past the largest finite `Float` is a lexer
  error.** A `FLOAT_LIT`, and the `DEC_PREFIX` of a `UNIT_LIT`
  ([LLEX.12]), reads as the `Float` nearest its value, ties to even
  ([LDET.3.2.8]). Where that value lies past the largest finite `Float`, so that
  it would round to an infinity, the compiler **must** refuse the literal as a
  lexer error, `"float literal out of range"`, with `DS_PARSE_FLOAT_RANGE`, as
  it refuses an integer literal out of range ([LLEX.11.1.5]). The compiler
  **must not** read such a literal as an infinity, and **must not** saturate it
  to the largest finite `Float`. A literal whose value rounds to zero is that
  zero. An infinity is written `inf` ([LEXP.4.2]).

  So `1.7976931348623157e308` is a literal, and `1.8e308` and `1e400` are lexer
  errors. So is the literal in `-1e400`, since a negative number is unary minus
  applied to a non-negative literal ([LGRA.2.7.6]).
